card.name: A 2‑storey, 7‑room colonial home with
card.summary: A 2‑storey, 7‑room colonial home with a large front porch, white clapboard siding, and gabled slate roof.
card.description: The two‑storey colonial residence rises 2.44 m per floor on a solid 20 cm concrete slab measuring 12.80 m by 9.91 m, capped by a gabled slate roof that adds a graceful 1.5 m pitch. Seven well‑proportioned rooms—four bedrooms, a living room, a dining room, a kitchen, and two full bathrooms—are arranged around a central hallway, each ceiling matching the historic 2.44 m height. The façade is clad in white wood clapboard, its crisp lines accentuated by black‑painted trim and double‑hung windows that slide open. A generous front porch spans the full 12.80 m width, extending 3 m outward with timber decking, a matching gable roof, and a pair of sturdy columns that invite lingering evenings. Interior walls are timber‑framed, insulated with fiberglass, and finished with plaster. Hardwood flooring runs beneath the living spaces, while the kitchen boasts custom oak cabinets and a farmhouse sink. All fixtures are period‑appropriate yet functional, from the ceramic toilets to the slate‑tiled bathtub. The house reads as a pure colonial statement, its proportions balanced, its porch commanding, and its craftsmanship evident in every detail, delivering a timeless home that feels both historic and livable.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions and verify the 1280 cm × 991 cm footprint with a 300 cm deep front porch.
Draft a full set of 2‑storey colonial floor plans showing 7 rooms, 2 bathrooms, and the big porch.
Obtain building permits and schedule trades for foundation, framing, roofing, and finishes.
Pour a reinforced concrete slab foundation and install the floor‑joist system for both levels.
Raise timber wall frames, sheathe, apply exterior wood clapboard siding, and install windows and doors.
Assemble roof trusses, sheathing, and slate shingles, then finish the porch roof and decking.
Complete interior finishes, install fixtures, perform a final inspection and hand over the house.
assumptions: The brief did not specify a garage, so the design omits one and leaves a driveway space for future addition.
Wall material is assumed to be wood clapboard painted white, a common finish for 1920s colonial pattern‑book homes.
Four bedrooms and two bathrooms are inferred from the typical room distribution of a 7‑room colonial plan.
The porch depth is taken as 300 cm to qualify as a "big" porch while remaining proportionate to the 12.80 m façade.

card.summary: A 2‑storey white‑clad colonial home with a large attached garage and a detached rear garage, built to 1920s pattern‑book proportions.
card.description: The two‑storey colonial residence measures 1585 cm by 838 cm and rises to a gable‑shingled roof that peaks at 200 cm above the second‑floor ceiling. White‑painted wood siding wraps the façade, punctuated by twelve double‑hung windows that slide open for fresh air. A generous front porch of 400 cm × 200 cm invites guests beneath a modest porch roof, while the main entrance door swings on sturdy hinges. Inside, three bedrooms, a sun parlor, and a full bathroom are arranged around a central hallway, all finished with hardwood flooring and plaster ceilings. The attached 2‑car garage occupies a 600 cm × 300 cm footprint on the side, its steel roll‑up door rising 210 cm to accommodate vehicles. At the rear, a detached garage of identical footprint provides additional storage or a workshop, accessed through a classic wood swing door. Structural timber framing, concrete foundation, and modern MEP services are concealed within the historic envelope, delivering a timeless yet functional home that respects the 1920s pattern‑book aesthetic while meeting today’s lifestyle needs.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions and set out the 1585 cm × 838 cm house footprint with a 300 cm setback for the detached garage at the rear.
Draft a full‑scale 2‑D plan showing the colonial façade, the 2‑car attached garage on the side, and the separate 600 cm × 300 cm garage positioned 300 cm behind the house.
Create a 3‑D BIM model in Revit, assigning LOD 100 for massing, LOD 200 for generic wall and roof geometry, and LOD 300 for detailed window, door, and structural members.
Coordinate trades by issuing structural, architectural, MEP, and garage‑specific sub‑drawings to the contractor, framing crew, electricians, plumbers, and roofers.
Construct the foundation, erect timber walls, install roof trusses, fit windows and doors, finish interior floors and ceilings, and complete both garage structures with their doors and services.
Perform a final inspection, verify all doors open on hinges, garage doors roll or swing, and certify that the detached garage is fully functional and compliant.
assumptions: The interior layout follows a typical colonial plan with a living room, dining room, kitchen, three bedrooms, and one full bathroom.
Standard double‑hung windows of 120 cm × 150 cm are used throughout to match the period style.
The roof pitch is assumed to be 6:12, giving a 200 cm rise over the 1585 cm span.
Interior finishes are assumed to be hardwood flooring and plaster ceilings unless otherwise specified.
questions: Do you prefer a specific roof material (asphalt shingles, wood shingles, or tile) for the gable roof?
What exact setback distance would you like for the detached garage behind the house?
Would you like any additional interior spaces such as a mudroom, pantry, or home office?

card.name: A two‑storey white‑clad colonial home with
card.summary: A two‑storey white‑clad colonial home with a large attached garage, a rear detached garage, and a living room staged with a big couch, coffee table, and TV.
card.description: The residence is a two‑storey New England colonial‑inspired home measuring 15.85 m (1585 cm) wide by 8.38 m (838 cm) deep, finished in white painted pine clapboard and capped with a steep gable roof of slate shingles. A generous front porch of 4 m × 3 m provides a welcoming transition from the driveway to the solid wood front door. The main block contains a central hallway, four bedrooms, two full bathrooms, and a spacious living room that anchors the front façade. An attached two‑car garage occupies the left side of the footprint, its steel roll‑up door sliding on a track, while a detached single‑car garage of 6 m × 3.5 m sits at the rear, linked by a paved side lane. Inside, the living room showcases a large sectional couch (250 cm × 100 cm × 90 cm) centered on a wool rug, a low glass‑top coffee table (120 cm × 60 cm × 45 cm) positioned directly in front, and a 140 cm wide flat‑screen TV mounted on a modest MDF stand. The interior walls are sheathed in drywall and painted white, with double‑hung wood‑frame windows providing natural light. All structural members are timber‑framed, the roof is supported by engineered trusses, and the house is equipped with a rooftop HVAC unit, a full electrical service panel, and a brick chimney serving a traditional fireplace. The design balances historic proportion with modern convenience, delivering a functional, elegant family home.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions, confirm setbacks, and produce a site‑plan that locates the main house, the large attached garage, and the detached rear garage.

Draft schematic floor plans showing two storeys, four bedrooms, two bathrooms, a central hallway, a front porch, and the interior layout of the living room where the big couch, coffee table and TV will be placed.
Develop detailed construction documents that include foundation footings, wood framing, roof trusses, garage door openings, and interior finish schedules.
Order all structural, finish, and furnishing materials and schedule trades for excavation, framing, roofing, MEP rough‑ins, and interior carpentry.
Erect the wood frame on the concrete slab, install windows, doors, garage doors, roof sheathing, and complete interior partitions, drywall, flooring, and finish carpentry.
Perform a final inspection, test all mechanical and electrical systems, and stage the living room with the couch, coffee table and TV for client hand‑over.
assumptions: Because the brief did not specify the number of stories, bedrooms or bathrooms, a typical 1920s pattern‑book layout of two storeys, four bedrooms and two bathrooms has been applied.
The wall material is assumed to be wood siding painted white, reflecting the common colonial finish in the reference designs.
A gable roof with slate shingles is chosen as a historically appropriate roof type for the style and period.
A front porch of 4 m × 3 m is added to give the house a balanced streetscape, as most colonial examples in the catalogue include a porch.
questions: Do you prefer the detached garage to be accessed via a side driveway or a rear driveway that passes behind the house?
Should the interior layout include a formal dining room or an open‑plan kitchen‑dining area on the first floor?
What specific finish or colour would you like for the interior walls and flooring beyond the default white paint and wood flooring?
